previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell degranulation syndrome, achalasia, and coronary artery disease s/p CABG was admitted for abdominal pain and a self-reported mast cell crisis. She presented with epigastric pain worsened by eating, chest tightness, flushing, and wheezing. Treatment followed her allergist’s protocol with IV methylprednisolone, Benadryl, and IV Dilaudid for pain. A CT abdomen showed no acute findings, and troponins remained negative, ruling out cardiac ischemia. She underwent an EGD with Botox injection at the gastroesophageal junction, which provided only transient relief. Her symptoms improved over three days with supportive care. Blood pressure-lowering medications were held due to hypotension during the crisis. She was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her allergist and GI specialist, continue oral symptom management, and restart chronic medications as advised by her providers.
